metadata.title: AzureRMADAppPermissionsReport
metadata.description:
Generate a full report of all applications your Azure AD has, including all permissions they require and how they have been assigned (user / admin), all to a nice tabulated Excel file.

Example run: get-azureRMADAppPermissionsReport -token (get-azureRMtoken -username jos.lieben@xxx.com -password password01) -reportPath c:\temp\report.xlsx

findings.title: Plain text is converted to a secure string
findings.description: File 'file-00002.psm1' uses ConvertTo-SecureString with plaintext. This will expose secure information. Encrypted standard strings should be used instead.

findings.title: Separate username and password parameters are declared
findings.description: Function 'get-azureRMToken' has both Username and Password parameters. Either set the type of the Password parameter to SecureString or replace the Username and Password parameters with a Credential parameter of type PSCredential. If using a Credential parameter in PowerShell 4.0 or earlier, please define a credential transformation attribute after the PSCredential type attribute.

findings.title: Plain text password parameter is declared
findings.description: Parameter '$Password' should not use String type but either SecureString or PSCredential, otherwise it increases the chance to expose this sensitive information.
